findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a client runs Jest or Vitest with an explicit worker count. The command receives its allocated budget here, but fasttest.node_worker_budget() preserves explicit --maxWorkers values unchanged (src/forge/fasttest.py:81–83). On eight cores, two worker sessions can each reserve two processes while each launches four workers, exceeding the shared four-process budget. Package scripts have the same gap. Admission must account for or enforce the actual runner allocation; setting FORGE_TEST_CPUS alone does not constrain these commands.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - running the repository's full test suite. tests/test_rules.py:49–53 rejects duplicate (STORY, criterion number) keys. This new function duplicates criterion 4 in test_machine_shared_test_budget.py. Both capacity functions also use criterion 2 with STORY="FIX-TWO-TEST-SLOTS", colliding with each other and the existing pane test. Consequently test_4_one_test_per_rule deterministically fails. Consolidate the cases under their owning tests while retaining their behavioral coverage.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - running the existing lane and upgrade tests. This assertion still requires a test-lane size of 1 on the six-core fixture, but test_slots() now returns 3. Two sibling assertions also retain the old doctor output: tests/test_lanes_upgrade.py:69 and tests/test_upgrade_doctor.py:85. The former is executed through test_lanes_tests.py's upgrade case. These tests deterministically fail under the new behavior; update all three expectations to the shared-process contract.
